usage: I take photos on the mountain
examples: I climb the mountain on weekends.
I breathed fresh air on the mountain.
There are really many mountains in Korea.
nuance: 산 is one of the most common nature words in Korea since the country is very mountainous, and people often say 등산 for hiking.
mistakes: Saying 산에서 가요 instead of 산에 가요 for going there.

examples: I want to go to the sea in summer.
I played with my friend at the sea.
nuance: 바다 means the sea or ocean and is a favorite summer destination, often paired with 해수욕장 for a swimming beach.
mistakes: Confusing 바다 (sea) with 바닥 (floor); they sound similar.

usage: I take a walk by the river
examples: I often go to the river in the evening.
I rode a bicycle by the river.
There is a big river in Seoul.
nuance: 강 means a river, and the Han River 한강 is a beloved spot in Seoul where people picnic, walk, and exercise.
mistakes: Writing 강에서 가요 instead of 강에 가요 when you mean going there.

examples: There are many trees in the park.
The trees are green in spring.
nuance: 나무 means a tree and also wood as a material, so the same word covers the living plant and lumber depending on context.
mistakes: Saying 나무가 와요 the way one says 비가 와요; trees do not use 오다.

examples: I gave flowers to my friend.
nuance: 꽃 means a flower and pairs with the verb 피다 (to bloom), so 꽃이 펴요 is the natural way to say flowers are blooming.
mistakes: Saying 꽃이 와요 instead of the correct 꽃이 펴요 for blooming.

examples: The grass in the park is green.
I sat on the grass and rested.
In spring the grass grows fast.
nuance: 풀 means grass or low plants and weeds, and the compound 풀밭 names a grassy field where people sit or play.
mistakes: Confusing 풀 (grass) with 풀 (glue); context tells them apart.

examples: There are many stones on the road.
The child picked up a stone.
nuance: 돌 means a stone or rock and appears in compounds like 돌담 for a stone wall, common in old Korean villages.
mistakes: Confusing 돌 (stone) with 돌 (first birthday); context separates them.

examples: I go to the island by boat.
I rested on the island for a few days.
nuance: 섬 means an island, and Korea has many such as 제주도, which adds the suffix 도 meaning island to its name.
mistakes: Saying 섬에서 가요 instead of 섬에 가요 when you mean going there.

usage: I ride a boat on the lake
examples: I went to the lake in the morning.
I saw ducks on the lake.
The water in this lake is clear.
nuance: 호수 means a lake, a calm body of water surrounded by land, and is a popular spot for walking and resting.
mistakes: Writing 호수에서 가요 instead of 호수에 가요 when you mean going there.

usage: I take a walk in the forest
examples: I want to go to the forest this weekend.
I heard birdsong in the forest.
This forest has very many trees.
nuance: 숲 means a forest or woods full of trees, and the compound 숲속 means deep inside the forest where it is quiet.
mistakes: Mixing up 숲 (forest) with 풀 (grass); they describe different things.

usage: there are many stars in the sky
examples: There are many stars in the sky at night.
Stars are seen well in the countryside.
nuance: 별 means a star and pairs with the verb 뜨다 (to rise), so 별이 떠요 is the natural way to say stars come out.
mistakes: Saying 별이 와요 instead of the natural 별이 떠요 for stars appearing.

usage: there is a moon in the sky
examples: The moon is bright in the night sky.
nuance: 달 means the moon and also a month, so the same word has two meanings, and it rises with the verb 뜨다 like the sun.
mistakes: Saying 달이 와요 instead of the natural 달이 떠요 for the moon rising.
